pr_title: Recover from default bridge init failure
pr_body:
**- What I did**

- fix https://github.com/moby/moby/issues/49291

If a bridge network can't be restored from the store on startup, then it's deleted, the daemon and bridge driver get out of step. If that happens to the default bridge, the daemon can't recover, it won't start again.

See the issue for more detailed description/analysis.

_The ipvlan/macvlan/overlay network drivers don't seem to be affected by an equivalent issue._

_This is a very long standing issue, but perhaps provoked by the checks on kernel module loading added in 27.x. (The version label on the PR is arbitrary, just something-old.)_

**- How I did it**

When deleting a network the bridge driver doesn't know about, make sure it's not still lurking in the data store.

**- How to verify it**

New tests.

**- Description for the changelog**
```markdown changelog
- Fixed an issue that could persistently prevent daemon startup after failure to initialize the default bridge.
```

issue_context.title: Error initializing Docker network controller: Conflict with existing bridge network docker0
issue_context.body:
### Description

- re-raised from https://github.com/docker/for-linux/issues/1512
- originally reported by @poqdavid

---

I'm encountering an issue with Docker on my Linux server where the Docker daemon fails to start due to a network conflict involving the default `docker0` bridge network. And I would appreciate it if anyone can help me figure out this problem.
Below are the details from the logs:

```
Dec 18 03:48:16 server dockerd[2720]: failed to start daemon: Error initializing network controller: error creating default "bridge" network: cannot create network e6df46e3462f284f46bb95fe8bdfa5530dfb1451b2859e886896fcecffe0f00a (docker0): conflicts with network 34958e77236c09db2c3cbe6198a3eb085736a648650638a1295480847abcf4b6 (docker0): networks have same bridge name
```

Here is the full log: [docker_log1.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/18190994/docker_log1.log)
Also my firewall log: [firewalld_log1.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/18191042/firewalld_log1.log)


**Steps to Reproduce:**
1. Start the Docker service on the affected system.
2. Observe that the daemon fails to start and the error above is logged.

**Temporary Fix:**
As a temporary workaround, I can resolve the issue by running the following commands:
```bash
rm -rf /var/lib/docker/network
systemctl restart docker
```
However, this fix is not permanent, and the issue reoccurs after some time.

**System Details:**
- Docker version: `27.4.1, build b9d17ea`
- Linux distribution: `Ubuntu 24.04.1 LTS`
- Kernel version: `6.8.0-51-generic x86_64`
- Firewall: `Firewalld 2.1.1 with nftables v1.0.9 (Old Doc Yak #3)`

**Update 1:**
After testing, a few things I noticed delaying the startup for the service fixes the problem but I am not completely sure if its a proper fix or not
```
[Unit]
PartOf=firewalld.service

[Service]
ExecStartPre=/bin/sleep 3
Restart=no
```
comments:
I think this happens when the daemon has been running normally, but it's failed to start up at-least once because of some issue while initialising the default bridge. Once that underlying issue is resolved, this error is reported on subsequent attempts to start up.

When it starts, the bridge network driver first tries to restore stored networks. If there's some issue causing the default bridge init to fail, it [deletes its in-memory ref to that network](https://github.com/moby/moby/blob/84bbd3badd305f0ad5cad1a7d951fe76a0986db0/libnetwork/drivers/bridge/bridge_linux.go#L850-L857). But, it's still in the datastore.

Config for the default bridge is normally [deleted and re-created](https://github.com/moby/moby/blob/84bbd3badd305f0ad5cad1a7d951fe76a0986db0/daemon/daemon_unix.go#L871-L888) when the daemon starts up, in case any of the daemon config that affects it has changed.

On the first restart where the old default bridge network has failed to restore, the daemon knows the default bridge network should already exist and deletes it, ready to re-create. But, the bridge driver thinks it doesn't exist (because it's dropped its in-memory ref). So, the network isn't actually deleted, but the daemon thinks it has been.

Then the daemon tries to create the replacement default bridge network, but it's likely to hit the problem that prevented the initial restore. So, the daemon fails to start, reporting whatever the underlying problem is with the bridge initialisation.

Next time the daemon starts, it won't try the delete, but it may still fail to create a new default bridge network. It'll report the underlying issue in this case too.

But ... when the underlying problem is resolved, and it's possible to start the default bridge driver again - the bridge driver successfully restores the network from its data store on startup. So, it has an in-memory ref for it.

The daemon still thinks there's no default bridge to delete, so it doesn't try - it just creates its new default bridge. But, for the bridge driver, the network does now exist. So, startup fails with the `networks have same bridge name` error.

My best guess is the sleep helps because, sometimes, something the daemon depends on sometimes isn't ready on the first try at starting up. When that happens, it's doomed, and the original cause of the startup failure won't be reported again. Waiting until whatever-it-is on the host is ready would make it start more reliably, avoiding the issue.

The problem isn't unique to the default bridge ... if a user-defined bridge network can't be restored on daemon startup, then the network is deleted by the user, the daemon and bridge driver get out-of-step in the same way.

In this case, there's no way to recycle the bridge name - but it's much less likely to be an issue because a user-defined network won't be automatically deleted by the daemon, the bridge name is random by default (`br-5dc5aaecc320`), and it won't prevent daemon startup.

review_comments:
This looks sane for now, but I went looking "didn't we already  have an options for this?", but that can only be used on `daemon.New()`;

```go
d := daemon.New(t, daemon.WithEnvVars(...)
```


and `daemon.Start()` doesn't take options as argument; perhaps we should consider making it accept Options, so that we can customise (some at least) daemon settings between restarts without having to create a new daemon.

Or perhaps a `StartWithOptions()` if we don't want  to replace the existing one (which takes  command-line arguments only)
